_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.
orderSource: the Handbook ranking control (scripts/handbook-shell.html), saved by Mike on 2026-08-15. It replaced design/mockups/to-do-list-table.html, which set the order before it.

items.name: Meeting Review — three non-coding gates before a first real recording
items.why: Mike asked for a feature that records a client meeting, transcribes it and produces two reports. It is built, advisor and manager both. What remains is three things only he or a lawyer can do.
items.risk: NO CODE IS OUTSTANDING. Three non-coding gates stand before a first real recording: staff consultation, a lawyer per market, and the OpenAI audio-terms letter - whose answers on training, retention and human review can falsify the spoken consent line. The declaration gate is built and live since 4.83 closed, so a firm that has not declared cannot start.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-01 — "i want you to design a new feature ... records the voices and transcribes the meeting, then generates two reports", quoted in full in meeting-review-history.md §1. He named the Handbook page himself, so the page is not an inference either.

items.touches: design/features/meeting-review.md and its history, design/MEETING-CONSENT-WORDING.md, design/ARTEFACTS.md, and the meeting routes, utilities, components and pages listed in the Brief's build table.
items.note: Built: observation points, consent and capture, transcription, audio destruction, the two reports, meeting-types slices 1-4, the MANAGER AGGREGATE (firm tier ALONE - P13), TRANSCRIPT EXPIRY on each meeting's own promised period, FOLLOW-THROUGH matched on the client, and the CLIENT COPY REQUEST - access, correction and early deletion. The CLIENT level of the pre-set is BUILT 2026-09-10 on the desktop (one shared list per client, every entry named, no manager screen - Mike's five rulings on the drawing). §4 ITEMS 3 AND 7 ARE CLOSED; THREE REMAIN and none is ours - staff consultation, the lawyer per market, and the OpenAI letter, SENT 2026-09-12 and awaiting reply. The /meeting-record banner is a real gate since 4.83 closed. Record: meeting-review-history.md §9.
items.comment: 2026-09-01 - filed; screens approved; slices 1-2 built. 2026-09-02 - slice 3, the types cascade, renumbered from 4.56; two rules Mike never made deleted (Brief P14). 2026-09-07 - the manager aggregate, transcript expiry and follow-through. 2026-09-08 - meeting-types slice 3 and slice 4's advisor half. 2026-09-10 - the impact assessment, which found IPP3A, new law since 1 May 2026 that no software can answer; then the Client Copy Request, drawn and built the same day on his instruction, closing §4 item 7. Two of its eight rulings reversed the recommendation: the advisor ALONE releases, so a request spanning several advisors is answered by each in turn. 2026-09-12 - the OpenAI letter sent; its reply closes DPIA finding A.

items.name: Adviser Network runs on nine invented people and forgets every decision in production
items.why: The people layer is an in-memory demo list. In production mode nothing persists, so a UAT tester meets invented advisers and every manager decision vanishes on restart.
items.risk: UAT judges a network that does not exist. Wiring our tables now would store ids nothing here can name: adviser identity belongs to Advisor-e and this app holds no advisers table. Not ours to fix until the master team answers question 7 of the integration email.

items.name: Learning from outcomes across consenting firms - the platform gets smarter with use
items.why: Case reviews already record how each template landed, and the engine reads that back for the same client only. Pooled across firms that consent, anonymised, it can adjust recommendations for everyone.
items.risk: Without it the product cannot honestly claim to get smarter with use beyond one client. The counter-risk is privacy: identifiers or client words leaving a firm, or a firm that never consented being changed by others' outcomes - both refused by the spec.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-10 - 'build a prompt to develop the task to enable real machine learning - such that it does, indeed, get smarter with use. Not just from one firm, but from all those who consent to help develop the model by sharing anonymised data'.

items.touches: caseStore.js template_outcomes and the mentor-share anonymiser, priorEngagement.js, the distinction-boost seam in templateResolver.js, the decision trace, a firm-tier consent tab and a Mentor Hub page in FirmManagerHub.vue, the overlay store at platform scope, the Scenario Lab.
items.note: SPEC KIT FEATURE, specs/002-outcome-learning. ALL BUILT AND POLISHED (2026-09-12): T001 to T047 ticked. The quickstart was walked on the desktop against local MySQL: consent, a pooled row with no free text, the mentor's decisions and both refusals, restore, both benches and the advisor's notice, all seen. It found and closed 4.94 (the trace named the wrong hold-back and could hide one). NOT SHOWN LOCALLY: a withdrawal taking an adjustment below the floor (yesterday's rows sit under a lost secret) and a second firm (one dev sign-in). Every word on both screens is ruled, on the drawings. Brief §8 says what stands where. WHAT REMAINS IS UAT.

items.name: Read this for me - plain guidance and an AI reading on the mentor's pages
items.why: Mike opened Outcome Learning and could not tell how to use it or what it was telling him; the client reports carry an AI reading and the hub pages carried none.
items.risk: A mentor who cannot read the page takes no decision on it, and the learning the platform gathered changes nothing. The counter-risk is a reading taken as a verdict, which the caveat under every reading and the backend's shape check answer.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-11 - 'I have no idea how I, as a mentor, am supposed to use this function and what I'm learning from it ... I'm not seeing any AI interpretation of what's in front of me. Is that possible we could create that?'

items.touches: components/shared/HubGuidePanel.vue and HubReadingCard.vue, both mentor pages, server/utils/hubReading.js, the two reading routes, the hub-reading document on the AI Prompts tab, locales.
items.note: BUILT 2026-09-11 from design/mockups/hub-page-guidance.html, approved the same day. Both pages open with How to use this page (Got it closes it, remembered per browser) and carry What this is telling you: on the button, never on open; the model is sent only what the page shows; a reply without the three fixed headings, or carrying a link or a name, is dropped whole; stored with the counts it was read from and marked stale when they move. It never accepts, holds or rejects anything. SEEN on the built app, failure message included: the model refused with 'no credits remaining' on the OpenAI account, Mike's to top up, so no real reading exists yet.

items.note: SPEC KIT FEATURE, specs/003-engine-middle-learning-true. US1, US2 AND US3 ARE ALL COMPLETE. US1: the engine proposes the primary issue, the advisor confirms or reframes, the Main issue row shows what was recorded - 25 of 51 cases propose, 96% survive the case's own words. items.comment: 2026-09-14 - filed on Mike's instruction after the audit comparison; spec, clarify, plan, tasks, four drawings and sixteen rulings the same day. TWO FAULTS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY TESTS: naming a problem from one category word, and recording plain agreement as a correction. THE SEED'S OWN DATA FLIPPED DIRECTION: Break-Even computed a hold-back of 4 and is in truth a lift of +2 - the engine was holding back what the pool recommended. items.name: A supplier-cost conversation is routed to sales and marketing
items.why: Domain detection put a client's supplier-cost problem in sales-marketing. The area decides which templates are even considered, so the advisor is offered sales and marketing tools for a margin problem.
items.risk: Every layer downstream inherits it and looks correct doing so - the templates, the primary issue, and the pooled row the platform learns from. Nothing on screen says the area may be wrong, and the advisor is only asked to confirm it once, in the engine's own words.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-14 - hit twice while walking 4.97 T018 on the running app. A defect we found, not a feature nobody asked for; Mike said yes to filing it.

items.touches: The domain keyword patterns in data/domains.json, the detection and disambiguation in server/advisorEngine.js, and the AI domain backstop that already exists beside them.
items.note: REPRODUCE: open the advisor, say 'margins are down, the cost of sales has gone up because suppliers put their prices up'. It lands in sales-marketing; under profit the same words score 4 on 'Cost of sales has increased'. The word 'sales' inside 'cost of sales' is the likely pull. NOT a primary-issue fault - that step is correct in both areas and is what made this visible.
items.comment: 2026-09-14 - filed at shutdown on Mike's yes, after the primary-issue step surfaced it. The 4.97 weak-evidence rule stops the engine NAMING a wrong problem here, but the wrong area stands.

items.name: A second opinion from two AI providers
items.why: Mike wonders whether two providers answering the same narrative or reading, with the advisor seeing both, gives a better answer than one. A later decision, separate from the fallback in 4.97.
items.risk: Without a decision it stays an idea. Building it doubles AI cost and wait on every call it covers, and a second provider needs the same privacy clearance as the first before any client words reach it.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-14 - 'perhaps there is a strength to using open AI AND Deepseek for the purposes of different perspectives?' Filed as its own item on his yes.

items.touches: The provider seam 4.97 builds, the narrative and hub-reading call sites, the advisor's screen where two answers would show, the provider clearance in config.
items.note: NOT PART OF 4.97. Needs a design decision first: which calls get two answers, what the advisor sees when they disagree, and which provider is cleared for which data. DeepSeek's China hosting and training terms are the privacy question to answer before it carries anything personal.
items.comment: 2026-09-14 - filed on Mike's yes so the idea is on the list and not in a chat.

items.name: No AI-backed script can run on the desktop
items.why: The certificate path in the desktop's .env points at a bundle that does not work there, so every OpenAI call from a script fails and the Scenario Lab cannot measure the AI layers.
items.risk: A lab run here silently reports the engine WITHOUT its AI layers and overwrites the report measured with them - score separation reads 2.3 against the real 5.7. Nothing says the layers were off unless someone reads the line that says so.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-14 - hit while measuring the resolver change for 4.97. A defect we found, not a feature nobody asked for; Mike said yes to filing it.

items.touches: .env on the desktop only (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), and scripts/scenario-lab.js which overwrites design/SCENARIO-LAB-REPORT.md whether or not the AI layers ran.
items.note: TWO PARTS. The environment half is known and recorded in memory: export the Avast Web Shield root and point NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS at it; certs/digicert-bundle.pem does NOT work on this machine and TLS is never disabled. The code half is ours and is the one that matters: the lab should REFUSE to overwrite the report when the AI layers did not run, or write to a clearly marked file, so a partial measurement cannot replace a full one.
items.comment: 2026-09-14 - filed at shutdown on Mike's yes, after a lab run without the key replaced a real report and was caught by the pre-commit hook rather than by anything in the lab itself.
